title: Contingencies and subsequent events — Reyes Corp.
instructions: Reyes Corp. is a private company with a December 31, Year 1 year-end. Its financial statements were **available to be issued on March 15, Year 2**. Evaluate each matter and review the draft note.

exhibits.title: Legal and other matters
exhibits.content:
1. **Product-liability suit** filed November Year 1 over a defect in units sold in Year 1. At December 31, counsel judged a loss probable, range $200,000–$500,000, no amount in the range better than another. On **February 20, Year 2**, the suit settled for **$350,000**.
2. **Warranties.** Year 1 sales were **$2,000,000**; warranty costs are estimated at 3% of sales. Year 1 warranty expenditures were **$25,000**. There was no beginning warranty liability.
3. **Suit against a competitor.** Counsel believes Reyes will probably be awarded **$150,000** in Year 2.
4. **Fire.** On **January 15, Year 2**, a fire destroyed an uninsured warehouse — estimated loss **$400,000**.
5. **Guarantee.** Reyes guaranteed a $1,000,000 bank loan of an affiliate in Year 1; the likelihood of payment is remote.
6. **Environmental claim.** A loss of about **$100,000** is reasonably possible.
7. **Nuisance claim.** An unasserted, unlikely-to-be-asserted claim with a remote chance of loss.

parts.prompt: Select the required treatment in the Year 1 financial statements.

rows.label: Product-liability suit
rows.explanation: Probable and estimable at year-end; the February settlement is a recognized (Type I) subsequent event.

rows.label: Warranties
rows.explanation: A probable, estimable obligation arising from Year 1 sales.

rows.label: Suit against a competitor
rows.explanation: Gain contingencies are not recognized until realized or realizable; adequate disclosure is required (ASC 450-30-50-1), without misleading implications.

rows.label: Warehouse fire
rows.explanation: The condition arose after year-end — a nonrecognized (Type II) event, disclosed because it is material.

rows.label: Guarantee of affiliate loan
rows.explanation: Guarantees are disclosed even when the chance of loss is remote.

rows.label: Environmental claim
rows.explanation: Reasonably possible losses are disclosed, not accrued.

rows.label: Nuisance claim
rows.explanation: An unasserted claim that is unlikely to be asserted with a remote loss needs neither.

rows.label: Litigation liability
rows.explanation: The settlement before the statements were available to be issued gives evidence of the year-end amount: **350,000** (not the 200,000 range minimum).

rows.label: Gain recognized on the suit against the competitor
